newsitem.title: USA: US December S&Ps end down after losing 13 pts late.
newsitem.headline: US December S&Ps end down after losing 13 pts late.

text.p: U.S. December Standard & Poor 500s finished sharply lower after losing 13 points in the last 30 minutes of pit trade.
"I suppose this action will make others want to lock in profits too," said Barrett Lewald, senior financial futures strategist with Lind-Waldock Inc.
Analysts said S&P futures, which rose nearly 11 percent in November, were long overdue for a correction to the downside.
"You had a meteoric rise in November, almost parabolic, so it would be healthy to see a sizable correction here," Lewald said.

December S&Ps' late slide came after the contract had held minimal losses earlier in the day. The slight setback in the U.S. bond market, as well as declines in the U.S. dollar against some currencies, softened S&P futures prices earlier.
However, once December fell through a critical support level of 752.80, the market hit heavy sell-stop orders and touched off technical sell signals, traders siad.
Within minutes, the contract was scraping below the key support level of 748.00, and dropped another 3.00 points to set an intraday low of 745.00.
Further support is seen at 737.00, the three-week low of 730.40 and 728.00. December S&Ps will retrace one-fourth of their 4-1/2-month upmove if they test the 728.00 level, analysts said.
"There are a lot of scared people," one S&P futures floor trader said. "When was the last time you saw anyone really afraid of this market?"
Traders and analysts also attributed year-end tax-related selling and a post-U.S. election selloff to the frenzied pace of sales in the pit.
The contract also narrowed its premium against the cash S&P index. December traded at or below the 0.60-point premium -- an area where arbitrage sell programs were expected to be hit.
Fair value was quoted by several traders at 1.35 to 1.50 points over cash, and arbitrage buy programs were seen at a 2.70- to 3.00-point premium to cash.
Midcap 400s and Nasdaq 100s, which held gains for most of the day, were not immune to the selling pressure in S&Ps. Both contracts dramatically reversed gains in sympathy with December S&Ps.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were 12.50 lower at 745.50, New Composites down 6.15 at 393.10, KBT Value Lines lost 4.90 at 681.90, Nikkeis fell 170.0 at 20,545, Midcap 400s were 1.15 lower at 257.30, and Nasdaq 100s dropped 12.75 points to 835.00.
